name: Fujitsu A64FX processor
description: Fujitsu designed the A64FX processor for the post-K supercomputer project that became Fugaku. It implemented Armv8.2-A with 512-bit SVE and combined vector processing cores with HBM2 memory in the package and a Tofu network interface on the chip.

date.basis: The archived Hot Chips 30 programme gives the scheduled day of Fujitsu's talk.

events.statement: Fujitsu presented the A64FX processor design, including the 512-bit SVE implementation, at Hot Chips 30 in Cupertino, California.

evidence.supports: Names A64FX, states its intended post-K role, and lists its architecture.

date.basis: RIKEN dates the announcement of the ranking to 18 November.

events.statement: RIKEN reported that a benchmarked Fugaku prototype at Fujitsu's Numazu plant used 768 A64FX processors.

evidence.supports: Distinguishes the operational prototype's processor count and location from the planned full installation.

earliest_record.rationale: The Hot Chips programme and design slides establish the dated disclosure. The later benchmark announcement documents working processors in a prototype system.

research.note: The link concerns SVE implementation in the A64FX. The recorded instruction benchmark ran on an FX1000 test system.

measures.quantity: Reciprocal throughput of standard SVE ld1d load

date.label: by 2021-07-30
date.basis: The inspected manuscript revision reports the measurements. The run date is unspecified.

measures.subject: Fujitsu A64FX in PRIMEHPC FX1000
measures.conditions: In-core instruction microbenchmark with the processor fixed at 2.2 GHz by default.

evidence.supports: Reports reciprocal throughput of 0.5 cycles for standard ld1d.

links.statement: Fujitsu implemented Arm's Scalable Vector Extension in A64FX using 512-bit vector registers. Fujitsu contributed to the SVE specification as an Arm lead partner.
links.scope: Instruction-set design and its implementation in the A64FX processor.

evidence.supports: The chip designer confirms collaboration and identifies the implemented instruction set and width.
Independent investigators report that the A64FX supports 512-bit SVE and benchmark specific SVE instructions on actual hardware.
